title: Ἄρκτος καὶ ἀλώπηξ
part: The Bear and the Fox (Chambry 63 · Perry 288)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 63 (= Perry 288). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἄρκος μεγάλως ἐκαυχᾶτο ὡς φιλάνθρωπος ὤν, ἐπεὶ νεκρὸν σῶμα οὐκ ἐσθίει· πρὸς ὃν ἡ ἀλώπηξ εἶπεν· « Εἴθε νεκροὺς εἷλκες, ἀλλὰ μὴ τοὺς ζῶντας. »
sentences.tr: Arkos megalōs ekauchato hōs philanthrōpos ōn, epei nekron sōma ouk esthiei· pros hon hē alōpēx eipen· « Eithe nekrous heilkes, alla mē tous zōntas. »
sentences.l: A bear was boasting greatly that he was a lover of men, since he does not eat a dead body; to whom the fox said: « If only you tore at the dead, and not at the living. »
sentences.i: A bear boasted loudly of being a friend to man, since he never eats a dead body; and the fox said to him: « I wish you would maul the dead, and leave the living alone. »
sentences.n: Ἄρκος is the later form of ἄρκτος, which the title still spells the old way. ὡς with the participle gives the boaster's own ground: 'on the plea that he was'. εἴθε with the imperfect indicative is a wish for the present that is not so — and εἷλκες is from ἕλκω, to drag or tear at, so the fox's point is that his abstinence costs him nothing: he kills the living instead.

sentences.t: Οὗτος ὁ μῦθος πλεονέκτας τοὺς ἐν ὑποκρίσει καὶ κενοδοξίᾳ βιοῦντας ἐλέγχει.
sentences.tr: Houtos ho mythos pleonektas tous en hypokrisei kai kenodoxiāi biountas elenchei.
sentences.l: This fable convicts of greed those who live in pretence and vainglory.
sentences.n: Another closing formula not among the usual ones: οὗτος ὁ μῦθος … ἐλέγχει. ἐλέγχω is the courtroom and Socratic word — to cross-examine a man until his claim collapses. πλεονέκτας stands predicatively with the verb: it shows them up as grasping. ὑπόκρισις is literally playing a part on the stage.
